title: Security: move VITE_BASE44_API_KEY out of the client bundle

done: base44/functions/proxyFetch/entry.ts — SSRF allowlist landed in commit 49d00bb (hostname + scheme)
src/api/base44Client.js + src/lib/AuthContext.jsx currently inject import.meta.env.VITE_BASE44_API_KEY as an `api_key` header on every request

problem: VITE_-prefixed env vars are inlined into the client JS bundle by Vite. Anyone who can download the built site can read the API key. A shared key is effectively a public key, defeating per-user auth and enabling abuse billed to the project.

steps.description: Add base44/functions/sessionExchange/entry.ts that mints a short-lived (e.g. 1h) session token bound to the authenticated base44 user. Stores the long-lived API key only on the server. Returns the session token to the client via an httpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax cookie.
steps.done_condition: POST /functions/sessionExchange responds 200 with Set-Cookie session=… httpOnly; fails 401 when upstream auth is invalid

steps.description: Update src/api/base44Client.js to rely on the session cookie (credentials: 'include') and stop reading import.meta.env.VITE_BASE44_API_KEY. The shared api_key header is removed from all client-side fetches.
steps.done_condition: grep 'VITE_BASE44_API_KEY' returns zero matches in src/; cookie-based auth works end-to-end

steps.description: Remove VITE_BASE44_API_KEY from .env and .env.example. Add a pre-commit hook that rejects any file containing VITE_.*_KEY= to prevent regression. Document the new flow in docs/adrs/ADR-020-client-side-api-key-remediation.md.
steps.done_condition: .env.example contains no VITE_*_KEY entries; ADR-020 lands; pre-commit hook blocks re-introduction

notes: Pair this with the SSRF fix (49d00bb) under a single 'auth hardening' arc. Together they close two of the three High findings from the 2026-04-14 swarm evaluation.
The third High finding (.env in git history) is out of scope here — needs a git-filter-repo pass coordinated with anyone holding unpushed branches.
